bugs.title: Error in OCEL parsing with empty relations
bugs.description: OCEL JSON files with no relationship data cause key error during parsing
bugs.technical_scope: Edge case handling in OCEL importer where empty dataframe sorting triggers error in classic.py line 149
bugs.business_value: Support for minimal OCEL files containing only objects and events without relationships
bugs.root_cause: Attempted to sort empty dataframe without checking if dataframe is empty first

bugs.title: pm4py.write.write_bpmn(...) produces invalid BPMN schema
bugs.description: BPMN export generates XML with schema violations: incorrect gatewayDirection capitalization and element ordering
bugs.technical_scope: Gateway direction attributes use lowercase (converging/diverging) instead of capitalized values per BPMN 2.0 spec; element ordering doesn't match validator expectations
bugs.business_value: Ensures exported BPMN models validate against standard BPMN 2.0 schema validators
bugs.root_cause: Implementation didn't follow BPMN 2.0 specification chapter 8.3.9 for gateway direction enumeration values

bugs.title: IMf determinism
bugs.description: Inductive Miner produces different Petri nets for identical input across Python versions and execution runs
bugs.technical_scope: Non-deterministic behavior in 'activity concurrent' fallthrough mechanism; structural differences (AND vs XOR gates) appear even with fallthroughs disabled
bugs.business_value: Reproducibility critical for research and production use cases requiring consistent model discovery
bugs.root_cause: Undeterminism in activity concurrent fallthrough logic; disable_fallthroughs parameter insufficient to guarantee determinism

bugs.title: pm4py.conformance.fitness_aligment crashing when using multiprocessing
bugs.description: BrokenProcessPool error when processing large event logs due to excessive memory consumption during alignment computation
bugs.technical_scope: Alignment algorithm visits numerous states consuming up to 32GB RAM; scipy compatibility issues with linprog integrality parameter
bugs.business_value: Enable conformance checking on large real-world datasets without memory crashes
bugs.root_cause: Alignment state space exploration consumes excessive memory; default variant not memory-optimized

bugs.title: xes_import.apply missed all time:timestamp values

bugs.technical_scope: Timestamp parsing issue affecting event log temporal data integrity

bugs.title: Dependency threshold from the Heuristics Miner produces strange results

bugs.root_cause: Pre-processing parameter dfg_pre_cleaning_noise_thresh must be set to 0.0 to prevent unwanted arc removal

key_insights.insight: Object-Centric Event Logs (OCEL) represent a fundamental paradigm shift from traditional case-based event logs. Traditional process mining algorithms expecting iterable trace structures cannot work directly with OCEL's object-centric data model, requiring specialized OCEL-aware algorithms.
action_items: Design UML behavioral models to handle object-centric perspectives, not just single-case traces
Support multiple object types with relationships in model representation
Ensure conversion operations preserve all relationships in object-centric structures
Consider MultiDiGraph structures for representing multiple relationships between same nodes
Handle edge cases like empty relationships gracefully in data import/export

key_insights.insight: Model conversions between different formalisms (BPMN ↔ Petri Net ↔ Process Tree ↔ DFG) are fraught with challenges: information loss, constraint violations, and semantic mismatches. Each formalism has different expressiveness and structural requirements.
action_items: Maintain explicit mappings between UML behavioral models and target formalisms
Document which constructs can and cannot be converted
Validate models after conversion to detect information loss
Support explicit join gateways for splits (BPMN best practice)
Ensure schema compliance when exporting to standard formats
Use lossless intermediate representations where possible
Preserve database constraints during export/import cycles

key_insights.insight: Process discovery algorithms like Inductive Miner suffer from non-determinism issues where identical inputs produce different outputs across runs and Python versions. This severely impacts reproducibility, a critical requirement for research and production systems.
action_items: Design discovery algorithms with deterministic behavior from the start
Use stable sorting and deterministic data structures
Provide random seed parameters for any stochastic components
Document which algorithms are deterministic vs non-deterministic
Test for reproducibility across environments as part of CI/CD
Version algorithm implementations separately from library versions

key_insights.insight: Alignment-based conformance checking faces severe scalability challenges with memory consumption and computation time. State space exploration can consume 32GB+ RAM and take 20+ minutes for moderate-sized logs. Alternative algorithms (token replay, Dijkstra variants) trade accuracy for performance.
action_items: Provide multiple conformance checking algorithms with different accuracy/performance trade-offs
Support memory-efficient variants like DIJKSTRA_LESS_MEMORY
Enable GPU acceleration for state space exploration where possible
Document computational complexity and memory requirements for each algorithm
Implement streaming/incremental conformance checking for large logs
Clearly document limitations of token replay (ignores activities not in model)

key_insights.insight: BPMN gateway semantics are frequently misunderstood. Inclusive gateways require explicit joins to match splits (unlike implicit AND joins). Token-based semantics differ from state-based analysis, affecting soundness and conformance checking.
action_items: Enforce BPMN best practices: explicit gateway joins for splits
Validate gateway pairing during model construction
Provide clear error messages explaining BPMN semantics violations
Support multiple conformance checking methods (token-based, state-based, alignment)
Document gateway behavior and semantics in user guides

key_insights.insight: Temporal data handling has multiple challenges: datetime range limitations (Pandas numpy.datetime64[ns] supports only 1677-2262), timestamp parsing failures, and performance metric granularity. Different date representations needed for different use cases.
action_items: Support multiple datetime representations with different ranges and precision
Validate timestamp ranges during import and provide clear error messages
Allow configurable time resolution for performance metrics
Handle timezone information consistently
Optimize timestamp parsing performance (avoid O(n²) algorithms)

key_insights.insight: Algorithm implementations and metrics evolve over versions, causing reproducibility challenges. PM4Py v2.2.13 vs v2.7.13.1 show significant precision metric differences due to algorithm improvements and bug fixes. Legacy API preservation balances innovation vs stability.
action_items: Version algorithms separately from library versions
Maintain legacy APIs alongside new implementations for reproducibility
Document breaking changes and metric calculation updates prominently
Provide migration guides for major version changes
Allow users to select specific algorithm versions explicitly
Tag research-reproducible versions with algorithm snapshots

key_insights.insight: Process mining algorithms have complex parameter interactions where preprocessing parameters can override or interfere with main algorithm parameters. The Heuristics Miner's dfg_pre_cleaning_noise_thresh default (0.05) can cause arcs to appear when threshold increases - counterintuitive behavior.
action_items: Document parameter interactions clearly
Use parameter groups/profiles for common configurations
Validate parameter combinations and warn about conflicts
Provide sensible defaults but allow full control
Use parameter builders to guide users through complex configurations

key_insights.insight: GPU acceleration through NVIDIA Rapids CuDF is integrated transparently - when CUDA is available, operations automatically execute on GPU without code changes. However, this requires careful dependency management and may not benefit all algorithms equally.
action_items: Design algorithms to benefit from GPU acceleration where possible
Support transparent GPU acceleration when hardware available
Provide CPU fallbacks for all GPU-accelerated operations
Document which operations benefit from GPU acceleration
Consider GPU memory constraints in algorithm design

key_insights.insight: Multiple event log formats coexist (XES, CSV, DataFrame, Legacy EventLog, Pandas-based EventLog, OCEL JSON, OCEL SQLite) each with different capabilities and limitations. Format conversion can lose information. DataFrame-based approach has datetime limitations but better performance for many operations.
action_items: Define canonical internal representation with maximum expressiveness
Document capabilities and limitations of each import/export format
Validate data integrity after format conversions
Support lossless round-trip where possible
Provide clear migration paths between formats
Consider using Apache Arrow for interoperability

key_insights.insight: Memory optimization often comes at significant speed cost. PM4Py's ITERPARSE_MEM_COMPRESSED reduced memory by ~50% but caused 5-10% slowdown on standard logs and catastrophic (8.7s → 45 min) degradation on logs with many attributes. User-controllable trade-offs needed.
action_items: Provide multiple algorithm variants with different memory/speed profiles
Default to speed-optimized variants with memory-optimized as option
Profile memory usage on diverse datasets during development
Document memory requirements and performance characteristics
Support streaming algorithms for memory-constrained environments
Allow users to choose trade-offs explicitly based on their constraints

key_insights.insight: API design has significant impact on correct usage. Using read_pnml() instead of read_bpmn() led to false soundness failures. Inconsistent naming conventions confuse users. Type-based dispatch and clear naming critical for usability.
action_items: Use type-based dispatch to call correct methods automatically
Provide clear error messages when wrong methods used
Maintain consistent naming conventions across API
Use domain-standard terminology aligned with literature
Provide high-level convenience functions for common workflows
Include type hints and runtime type checking

architectural_decisions.decision: Pandas DataFrame as Primary Event Log Representation
architectural_decisions.rationale: Leverage Pandas ecosystem for data manipulation with better performance than object-oriented EventLog, despite datetime range limitations
architectural_decisions.impact: Significant performance improvements for data operations but datetime limitations (1677-2262); legacy EventLog maintained for compatibility

architectural_decisions.rationale: Enable GPU acceleration without requiring user code changes by detecting CUDA availability automatically
architectural_decisions.impact: Significant performance gains on GPU hardware while maintaining CPU compatibility; increased dependency complexity

architectural_decisions.rationale: Revert from ITERPARSE_MEM_COMPRESSED after discovering catastrophic performance degradation on certain logs
architectural_decisions.impact: Restored parsing performance (400-500 it/s vs 5-20 it/s); accepts higher memory usage for reliability

architectural_decisions.rationale: Provide memory-optimized (DIJKSTRA_LESS_MEMORY) and speed-optimized variants of expensive algorithms like alignments
architectural_decisions.impact: Users can choose appropriate trade-offs for their constraints; increased API surface area

architectural_decisions.rationale: Support wider date ranges and ensure reproducibility for existing research despite moving to Pandas-based approach
architectural_decisions.impact: Increased maintenance burden but better backward compatibility and date range support

architectural_decisions.rationale: Support emerging object-centric process mining paradigm requiring new algorithms and data structures
architectural_decisions.impact: Enables object-centric process mining but fragments API between traditional and OCEL approaches

architectural_decisions.rationale: Fix BPMN export to comply with BPMN 2.0 specification for gatewayDirection capitalization and element ordering
architectural_decisions.impact: Ensures interoperability with other BPMN tools through standards compliance

architectural_decisions.rationale: Follow BPMN best practices requiring inclusive gateway splits to have matching joins rather than implicit joins
architectural_decisions.impact: Prevents modeling errors but requires users to understand BPMN semantics

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Design UML behavioral models to natively support object-centric perspectives with multiple interrelated object types, not just single-case traces. Support multiple concurrent objects participating in behaviors.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: OCEL represents fundamental shift from case-based to object-centric process mining. Traditional algorithms cannot work with OCEL without adaptation. Object-centric thinking must be built into model representation from the start.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Design conversion system with explicit capability matrices documenting what can/cannot be converted between formalisms. Validate after conversion and report information loss. Consider intermediate canonical representation.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Every format conversion in PM4Py has issues: BPMN→Petri net, Petri net→Process Tree, OCEL→NetworkX. Information loss, constraint violations, and semantic mismatches are pervasive. Need architectural approach to handle conversion fidelity.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Ensure all discovery and transformation algorithms are deterministic with reproducible results. Use stable sorts, deterministic data structures, random seeds for any stochastic components. Test reproducibility in CI/CD.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Inductive Miner non-determinism severely impacts reproducibility. Same input produces different outputs across Python versions and runs. Reproducibility critical for research and production use.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Design model validation and conformance checking with scalability in mind. Provide multiple algorithms with different accuracy/performance trade-offs. Support memory-efficient variants and GPU acceleration where possible.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Alignment-based conformance checking can consume 32GB+ RAM and take 20+ minutes for moderate logs. State space explosion is fundamental challenge. Multiple algorithm variants with clear trade-off documentation essential.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Use MultiDiGraph or similar structures to represent multiple relationships between same elements when needed. Critical for object-centric models where multiple relationships exist from different perspectives.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: OCEL conversion to NetworkX loses DF relations because DiGraph supports only one edge between nodes. Multi-perspective models need multi-edge support.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: For BPMN-like control flow, enforce best practice that gateway splits must have matching joins. Validate gateway pairing during model construction with clear error messages.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Inclusive gateway splits without explicit joins violate BPMN best practices and cause soundness issues. Explicit join enforcement prevents modeling errors.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Support multiple datetime representations with different ranges and precision. Don't rely solely on Pandas datetime64[ns] which limits to 1677-2262. Allow configurable time resolution for performance metrics.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Pandas datetime limitations prevent processing historical or far-future dates. Different use cases need different temporal precision (milliseconds to days).

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Version algorithms separately from library versions. Allow users to specify algorithm version explicitly for reproducibility. Document algorithm changes prominently in changelogs.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: PM4Py precision values differ significantly between versions due to algorithm improvements and bug fixes. Research reproducibility requires ability to use specific algorithm versions.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Validate parameter combinations and warn about conflicts or interactions. Document parameter dependencies clearly. Consider parameter builders for complex configurations.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Heuristics Miner preprocessing parameter can override main algorithm threshold in counterintuitive ways. Complex parameter interactions need explicit documentation and validation.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Use type-based dispatch and runtime type checking. Provide clear error messages when wrong methods used on wrong types. Include comprehensive type hints.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Users called read_pnml() instead of read_bpmn() leading to false soundness errors. Type-safe APIs prevent misuse.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: When exporting to databases or structured formats, preserve constraints (primary keys, foreign keys, uniqueness). Don't rely solely on Pandas for export if it loses constraints.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: OCEL 2.0 export via Pandas loses all database integrity constraints (11 constraint violations after round-trip). Need explicit constraint preservation.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: For expensive algorithms, provide variants with different memory/speed profiles. Default to speed-optimized with memory-optimized as explicit option. Document resource requirements clearly.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: ITERPARSE_MEM_COMPRESSED caused 8.7s → 45min degradation on certain logs despite 50% memory reduction. Users need control over trade-offs.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: When exporting to standard formats (BPMN, PNML, etc.), validate against official schemas. Test interoperability with other tools.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: PM4Py BPMN export had schema violations (wrong capitalization, element ordering) preventing validation with standard tools. Standards compliance critical for interoperability.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Use consistent naming across modules and align with domain-standard terminology from literature. Avoid naming conflicts or similar names for different concepts.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: PM4Py had naming inconsistencies across objects and visualization modules. Consistent terminology improves usability.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Handle edge cases like empty collections, single elements, missing optional data gracefully without crashes. Validate inputs and provide clear error messages.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Empty OCEL relations caused crashes. Single activity in OCDFG visualization failed. Edge cases need explicit handling.
